events.asset: Global antidepressant prescription volume (antidepressants, ATC N06A), calendar year 2026 versus 2025
events.entity: IQVIA (publisher of the global prescription audit)
events.title: Global antidepressant prescription volume falls in 2026 versus 2025
events.proposition: Global antidepressant prescription volume for calendar year 2026 is below the volume for calendar year 2025, per IQVIA's global data.
events.criterion: Resolved on IQVIA global antidepressant volume data only (IQVIA MIDAS, as published by IQVIA or the IQVIA Institute in its global medicine-use reports). TRUE if the published global antidepressant volume for calendar year 2026 (prescriptions, or the report's standard-unit or defined-daily-dose measure for antidepressants, ATC N06A) is lower than the published figure for calendar year 2025 in the same series and unit; FALSE if it is equal or higher. A direction resolves as binary at the prior-year value. Regional or single-country series do not count. If the series has not published both years' values 12 months after the deadline, the event is unresolvable.

resolution_source.name: IQVIA global antidepressant volume (IQVIA MIDAS), as published by IQVIA or the IQVIA Institute

quantity.metric: global antidepressant prescription volume (antidepressants, ATC N06A) for calendar year 2026, compared with the calendar-2025 value in the same series
quantity.unit: prescriptions or standard units, year total
quantity.series: IQVIA MIDAS global antidepressant volume, calendar years 2025 and 2026, as published by IQVIA or the IQVIA Institute

readings: 'Antidepressant prescriptions' is read as dispensed antidepressant volume in the unit the series publishes.
'Globally' = the worldwide total, so only a global series resolves the event.
'For the first time' is historical framing and is not scored; the direction is judged against 2025 only.

related_timeline.event: FDA grants 510(k) clearance to Magnus Medical's SAINT Neuromodulation System (MRI-guided accelerated TMS) for MDD in adults who failed prior antidepressants.
related_timeline.key_number: ~80% remission vs 13% control in pivotal data

related_timeline.event: Usona launches phase 3 uAspire: single 25 mg psilocybin dose vs placebo in about 240 adults with MDD, 6-week blinded period and 1-year follow-up.
Done Global CEO Ruthia He and clinical president David Brody are arrested on federal charges over an alleged $100M Adderall telehealth distribution scheme.
MHPAEA final rule published (released September 9): NQTL comparative-analysis and meaningful-benefit requirements, effective November 22, 2024, applicable plan years 2025 and 2026.
Compass delays COMP005 topline to Q2 2025 and COMP006 data to after the 26-week point (H2 2026) to protect blinding, and lays off 30% of staff.
Third temporary extension of telemedicine flexibilities for controlled medications through December 31, 2025.
VA awards up to $1.5M over five years for its first VA-funded psychedelic study: MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD and alcohol use disorder at Providence and West Haven VAs.
CY2025 PFS final rule published; CMS keeps telehealth policies under its own authority (audio-only, virtual supervision) while statutory Medicare telehealth flexibilities await Congress.
Colorado begins accepting natural medicine business license applications; the regulated program launches January 1, 2025.
DEA's chief ALJ cancels the January 21, 2025 marijuana rescheduling hearing pending an interlocutory appeal; the proceeding stalls.
related_timeline.source_org: Ohio State Moritz College of Law (DEPC)

related_timeline.event: DEA publishes proposed rule creating special registrations for telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances; comments closed March 18, 2025 with 6,400+ received.
DEA and HHS delay the effective date of the buprenorphine and VA telemedicine final rules to December 31, 2025 after an earlier delay to March 21, 2025.

events.asset: Accelerated TMS (more than one session per day, such as accelerated iTBS or SAINT/SNT protocols) in outpatient clinics
events.entity: A US health payer with national scope (a national commercial insurer or a federal program)
events.title: A national US payer covers accelerated TMS in the outpatient clinic setting
events.proposition: A US health payer with national scope covers accelerated TMS delivered in outpatient clinics, through a published coverage policy or a publicly announced pilot or network agreement.
events.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of (a) a published medical policy, bulletin or fee schedule of a US health payer with national scope (a national commercial insurer or a federal program) that lists an accelerated TMS protocol (more than one session per day, e.g. accelerated iTBS or SAINT/SNT) as covered or medically necessary in an outpatient clinic, or (b) a public announcement by such a payer, alone or with a provider, of a pilot or network agreement that pays for accelerated TMS in outpatient clinics. Once-daily TMS coverage, trial-only coverage, case exceptions, a single-state or regional plan, an unpublished contract, or inpatient-only coverage does not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such policy or announcement is dated by then. Resolution source: the payer's policy bulletin or fee schedule, or the payer's or provider's press release for the agreement.

resolution_source.name: The payer's published medical policy bulletin or fee schedule; payer or provider press release for a pilot or network agreement

readings: 'or Accelerated TMS' is read as 'for Accelerated TMS' (typo), per the finder and the sentence structure.
'A national payor—or two' = at least one payer with national scope; a single-state or regional plan does not count.

'It won't be broad—it will start with pilots and narrow network deals': the forecaster counts pilots and narrow network arrangements as coverage, so a publicly announced pilot or network agreement satisfies the event.

'Accelerated TMS' = protocols with more than one TMS session per day (accelerated iTBS, SAINT/SNT-type), as in the related proposals new:uhc-covers-accelerated-tms-depression and new:additional-health-plan-covers-accelerated-tms.
'We' is read as accelerated-TMS providers, which include the forecaster's employer Radial.

events.asset: Professional-society guidance against antidepressants other than fluoxetine for depression in children and adolescents
events.entity: American Academy of Pediatrics, American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, or another pediatric-care society
events.title: A pediatric or child-psychiatry society warns against non-fluoxetine antidepressants for youth depression
events.proposition: A professional society for children's health care issues a warning, policy statement or clinical guideline that recommends against prescribing antidepressant medications other than fluoxetine for depression in children and adolescents.
events.criterion: TRUE on the publication date of an official policy statement, clinical practice guideline, clinical report or public warning issued by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (AACAP), or another professional society whose members care for children or adolescents, that recommends against, or advises clinicians not to prescribe, antidepressants other than fluoxetine for depression in children and/or adolescents, as shown by the document text. A guideline that ranks fluoxetine first while still endorsing other antidepressants, a statement about a single drug, an individual member's editorial, or an FDA action does not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such document has been published by then. Resolution source: the issuing society's official publication or website (AAP: Pediatrics, aap.org; AACAP: JAACAP, aacap.org).

resolution_source.name: The issuing society's official publication or website (AAP: Pediatrics, aap.org; AACAP: JAACAP, aacap.org)

readings: 'All drugs (except prozac) for depression in youth' = antidepressant medications other than fluoxetine, for depression in children and adolescents.
'A warning (or stern guideline)' = a formal society document that recommends against such prescribing; ranking fluoxetine first while still endorsing alternatives does not count.
'AAP, AACAP, or the like' = any professional society for children's care ('A or B' is one event).

events.asset: At-home (home-use) depression treatment devices legally marketed in the United States (count of devices)
events.entity: US Food and Drug Administration (device authorizations) and the device sponsors (commercial availability)
events.title: Three or more at-home depression treatment devices on the US market
events.proposition: By the period end, three or more distinct hardware devices with an FDA authorization naming a depressive disorder indication and home use are commercially available in the United States, per FDA device databases and sponsor availability announcements.
events.criterion: Resolved on FDA device authorization records and sponsor announcements only. Count the distinct hardware devices that, at the period end, (a) hold an FDA marketing authorization (510(k) clearance, De Novo grant or PMA approval, per the FDA 510(k), De Novo and PMA databases) whose indications for use name a depressive disorder (major depressive disorder or depression) and home use or use outside a clinical setting, and (b) are commercially available to patients in the United States per the sponsor's public announcement (press release or product website). TRUE if the count is three or more; FALSE otherwise. Devices marketed for depression without such an authorization, software-only products, and devices authorized only for in-clinic use do not count. quantity.metric: number of distinct at-home depression treatment devices legally marketed in the US (FDA home-use depression authorization plus commercial availability)

events.asset: New federal criminal cases against companies selling or prescribing controlled substances (Done Global-type cases)
events.title: At least two new federal criminal cases against companies selling controlled substances
events.proposition: US federal prosecutors bring at least two additional criminal cases, of the kind brought against Done Global, against companies (or their principals) for selling or prescribing controlled substances.
events.criterion: TRUE on the docket date on which the second qualifying case is filed. A qualifying case is a federal criminal case (indictment, information or complaint) filed after the statement date by US federal prosecutors against a company that sells or prescribes controlled substances (manufacturer, distributor, pharmacy, or telehealth or clinic prescriber), or against its principals, on charges about that sale, distribution or prescribing, as in the Done Global prosecution. events.asset: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) for depression in adolescents: health plan coverage
events.entity: US health plans other than UnitedHealth Group (UnitedHealthcare) and Cigna

events.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of a published medical policy or coverage bulletin from a US health plan (commercial or public), other than UnitedHealth Group/UnitedHealthcare and Cigna, that newly lists transcranial magnetic stimulation as covered or medically necessary for major depressive disorder in adolescents (an age range that includes patients under 18), where the plan's policy in force on 2026-01-05 did not cover TMS for patients under 18, as shown by the policy's revision history or the prior policy text. readings: 'Other plans will follow' = at least one additional US health plan adopts adolescent TMS coverage; the countable set is US health plans with a published TMS policy, baseline the plans covering adolescents on the statement date (UnitedHealth Group, Cigna, 'Medical' and 'more', per the forecaster).
